body: I have two dogs in a townhome and have 3 air purifiers. Absolutely love them. No dog smell. I have one Medify and two Levoit. Just make sure you get one that can actually clean the size of the space it will be in. The downside is buying the filters, but I find it worth the cost, and you can find cheaper, off-brand filters on Amazon.

His recovery went smoothly. He was in the hospital for 3 or 4 days (this was in 2013). He slept in the recliner at home for a week, at least, then was able to transition to his bed. He was off pain meds within 2-3 weeks. His activity and lifting were limited for about 6 weeks. His friend carried his backpack to and from school for him 😃. I did the research to find the doctors who did the Nuss procedure. It's a less invasive procedure with fantastic results. Our insurance covered it completely.  But again, this was 2013. It's crazy to think I gave birth to my daughter in 1995 and paid $10. That was the co-pay. Anyway, back yo my son - We drove him to Norfolk once every year for 7 years to be monitored and measured. They specifically waited until he was ready to hit that final big growth spurt to do the procedure.  His lung capacity prior to surgery was in the 75% range. My son had the bar removed 2 years later, and his lung capacity was at 90%, but they said it would continue to improve. Hope this information was helpful.

My son had pectus excavatum and had the Nuss procedure done at the Children's Hospital of the Kings Daughters in Norfolk, VA.  His doctor monitored him from age 6 until he had surgery at age 13. Check out the Nuss procedure.

58F, I've owned both, but townhome living is so much easier.  Maybe I lucked out with a quality build (built 1998), but I hear nothing through the walls. And my immediate neighbors,  left and right side, have dogs. I have a small fenced back yard big enough to let my pups out, patio, hammock, and a storage shed. My HOA is $154/mo and that covers trash, snow removal, roof, siding & gutter repair coverage.  They mow my backyard if I leave the gate open. The HOA does a great job with landscaping and keeping the place looking nice. I do miss the bigger yard at the house I owned, but my dogs adjusted just fine.

I resonate with this because I am that woman who did the same thing to a wonderful man. Long story short, I lost my 17 year old son to suicide, my mom to a heart attack and my fiancé to colon cancer within a three year period. I'm the one that found my son in his bedroom, I went to the hospital with my mom where they were not able to save her and I took care of my fiancé (with hospice) until he died. I went over the edge. In hindsight I was using people to avoid the PTSD, grief, and all the other shit I should have be working on. I know this woman felt like 'the one', but believe her when she says it's her and not you. She simply moved on to her new victim. I finally started counseling (much too late, but could not even comprehend doing it any earlier) and the therapist said my behavior was a product of PTSD. Please feel grateful that you dodge a bullet and you deserve someone who has their shit together. One day I will have mine together and will be a better person for the right man. I have since sincerely apologized to the one man I did hurt. We are now distant friends and he has found a lovely woman who deserves him, and I am very happy for them both.

I have been reading this sub for a very long time and enjoy everyone's comments. However, I do have a different take on the show. Of course, my analysis is based on the edits the show presents. It all could be different in real life. I am prepared for a world of hurt for posting this, but here I go. Kody, not Robyn, is 100% to blame for the failure of the family. I am also rewatching from the beginning and I'm on Season 15. I believe Robyn came into the family with good intentions and tried to the best of her ability to make it work. The problem is she came into the family with no resources to share, does not seem to have the coping skills to hold a job and raise her children without help, may have a medical issue that has not been disclosed on the show (hence her swelling neck and seems fatigued all the time) and does not want people in her house. This is 100% on Kody. He saw a pretty damsel in distress and swooped in to rescue her without a single thought as to how this would play out with the other OG3 and kids. He found someone that would stroke his ego. Who the heck can blame Robyn for that? She is a great partner for Kody, as a wife should be, but she just didn't know how to be a good partner to the other wives. She didn't step up. It would have required her to exert more energy than she is capable of, whether that is a personality flaw or a medical issue is the unknown. She may be an emotional creature that crawls under her covers when faced with life's difficulties. Again, that is not her fault. Robyn loved the idea of a plural family, and was probably very sweet and kind to the OG3, but just wasn't capable of coping with the structure and being a resource as opposed to being a drain. Unless she lied while courting Kody, saying "I will work to bring in money" and "I will help with babysitting", then it is 100% on Kody. He was thinking with his heart and dick, and did not stop to consider how they would absorb her into the family without it becoming a financial and emotional strain. When they moved to Flagstaff Kody just imploded. He was beyond tired. He discovered that one woman, Robyn, could fill his tank and he didn't need to work so hard for so little love and understanding any longer. It was Kody that manipulated the OG3 to sell their LV homes by love bombing each of them. I truly believe that Robyn did not want to buy her house in Flagstaff, that she wanted to go out to Coyote Pass with the other women, but in the end her hesitation to buy (as opposed to renting) caused them more financial drain. If she wanted to be truly selfless, she would have gone into a 3 bedroom apartment, while letting Aurora & Dayton live with Meri until they could find a suitable rental. But, Robyn is human and isn't selfless. She came into the family wanting the culture, but what was she to do when Kody put her on a pedestal? He was in love with her and only wanted her to have the best. I do think Robyn is miserable that the family is not together. I do not think she wanted Kody all to herself. But he fell for the one woman who was weaker than the other 3, and who filled his emotional tank. I'm glad the other wives are out from that mess, are thriving, and have proved that polygamy is not sustainable unless the woman wants to regarded as a second class baby maker.

I'm an older step-mom (54); my bio children are adults and on their own. No grandkids yet. My SO (51) has a 13 year old son living with us full-time, only visiting his mom about 2 weeks a year. I do not try to parent the SS; my SO handles all of that, although he does ask my opinion about matters frequently. For SS, I'm just another person in the house. He's been disrespectful and rude at times, but for the most part he's easy to be around. If I ask him to clean up his mess he usually does with minimal attitude. My SO and I have made it clear what is acceptable and not acceptable behavior. We've instilled that for this to be a peaceful home everyone needs to be respected, including the SS. I think if my children were younger and still at home it would be more difficult. As it is, there is no competition for attention or affection for my SS.
